newsitem.title: USA: Volatile market scared off investors in December.
newsitem.headline: Volatile market scared off investors in December.

text.p: Several mutual funds expect a healthy rise in January cash inflows as investors return after pulling out from the volatile stock market in December.

Net new cash into U.S. stock funds declined to an estimated $13.5 billion in December from $17.1 billion in November, and $16.39 billion in December 1995, said the Investment Company Institute, an industry trade group.
The Dow Jones industrial average suffered declines in the first two weeks of December, then had two weeks of increases, before ending about 72 points lower for the month.

"The estimated slowing of flows in December likely reflects the volatility of the stock market in early December," as well as investors deferring purchases until funds completed year-end dividend and capital gains distributions, the trade group said.

Charles Schwab Corp. saw a "strong surge of activity" in the first 10 days of this month, with $653 million in net flows into equity funds vs. $60 million for all of December, according to a spokeswoman.
The strongest flows were into international and global equity funds, with about $225 million in January vs. $48 million in December.
Index funds were also popular, with $120 million vs. $81 million in December.

"It could be that people tend to hold their powder while they figure out taxes for next year," said spokeswoman Tracey Gordon. "In January, people look at the market and say, 'I'm getting in.' There's also a lot of bonus money, year-end money going to work."

T. Rowe Price Associates Inc. spokeswoman Rowena Itchon said "January so far was very good," with strong flows into its equity income, blue chip growth, growth and income, and international stock funds.
Michael Lipper, president of Lipper Analytical Services, a fund research firm, said he expected flows for the first five months of this year to fall below year-ago levels.

"December and January are going to be down because the flows coming from 401(k) (pension) money were so large last year, and a good bit of that were (pension) conversions rather than normal flows," said Lipper. "It's not looking good for comparisons for perhaps the first five months."
Charles Biderman, editor of the Mutual Fund Trim Tabs newsletter, said he feared that the U.S. stock market, accustomed to the benefits of monthly flows of around $20 billion, could be disappointed.
Biderman said he believed that $15 billion per month in flows "would be more sustainable" this year.
